p: Which chart best compares total waiting minutes across three clinics?
why: Bars compare a small number of separate categories.

p: Which preparation is essential before plotting weekly change?
c: Sort the week values in their real order
Replace every missing week with zero
why: A line chart requires meaningful order and visible gaps.

p: What does one point represent in a scatter of patients_seen against average_wait_minutes from the source table?
why: Scatter pairs two quantities from the same observational unit.

p: Which chart examines the distribution of one numeric variable?
why: A histogram counts values in adjacent numeric intervals.

p: Why display the plot table before drawing?
c: To inspect the exact values and grain encoded by the chart
why: The chart remains traceable to inspected values.

p: What should normally be true of the length axis in a category bar chart?
c: It begins just below the smallest value
why: Bar length encodes magnitude, so a zero baseline prevents exaggeration.

p: Which label is complete for total waiting burden?
why: The label names both the measure and unit.

p: A monthly series has no March record. What should the analyst do first?
c: Expose the gap and investigate it
Convert March to zero without explanation
Join February and April and claim continuity
why: Missing observation is not the same as observed zero.

p: Which statement about a scatter plot is correct?
c: It can show association but does not establish cause
It proves the x value caused y
It must use category names on both axes
why: Observed relationships need further evidence before a causal claim.

p: Which check directly validates a clinic-level plot table?
c: Its totals reconcile with the analysis records
why: Numerical reconciliation checks that aggregation did not lose or duplicate records.
